segments.text: Discovered by Karl Wilhelm Feuerbach in eighteen twenty-two, X eleven is the Feuerbach Point: the celebrated point where the incircle centered at X one and the nine-point circle centered at X five kiss in internal tangency.

subsegments.text: Discovered by Karl Wilhelm Feuerbach in eighteen twenty-two, X eleven is the Feuerbach Point: the celebrated point where the incircle centered at X one and the nine-point circle centered at X five kiss in internal tangency.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Its trilinear coordinates are one minus cosine of B minus C, to one minus cosine of C minus A, to one minus cosine of A minus B, with algebraic barycentrics s minus a times b minus c squared. Because the point of tangency of two circles always lies on their line of centers, X eleven lies directly on the Feuerbach line through X one, X five, and X twelve.

segments.text: X eleven is the harmonic conjugate of X twelve with respect to X one and X five, the isogonal conjugate of X fifty-nine, and lies on the circumcircle of the intouch triangle and the pedal circle of the Spieker center.
